description: A team powered by delusion, audacity, and just the right amount of craziness. We may not know what we’re doing, but somehow, we convinced ourselves that we can do it.
summary:
Space Archaeologist is an educational 3D browser game designed for children aged 7–12, transforming NASA’s space exploration history into an interactive adventure. Players become space archaeologists, investigating historical equipment left on the Moon and Mars, including Apollo 11 artifacts and NASA’s Opportunity rover.

Through immersive 3D exploration, artifact investigations, experiments, quizzes, and mission-based activities, players discover the scientific value and stories behind these machines. The game also features Nova, an AI-powered guide that answers space-related questions through voice or text using curated, sourced information. Accessibility features include narration, captions, customizable explorers, multiple control options, and optional hand-tracking interactions.

The project addresses the challenge by preserving and presenting NASA’s space heritage in an engaging, child-friendly learning experience. Supported by 275 curated fact lines and 46 reference sources, primarily from NASA, Space Archaeologist encourages scientific curiosity, critical thinking, and appreciation for the technologies that made space exploration possible. It demonstrates how interactive technology can make space science more accessible and inspire the next generation of explorers.
details:
pace Archaeologist is an educational 3D browser game designed for children aged 8 to 11. It introduces players to the history and scientific value of equipment NASA left on the Moon and Mars. Through exploration and storytelling, the game presents these machines as artifacts that preserve stories of human discovery, helping young learners connect with space science.

Set within an imagined future, Space Archaeologist lets players become explorers investigating historical space equipment. Players create an avatar, board a spacecraft, and choose a mission. On the Moon, they investigate Eagle’s descent stage, a laser reflector, a seismometer, and a commemorative plaque before collecting samples, reconstructing the mission, and completing a report. On Mars, they follow Opportunity’s story and manage its solar energy in the Sol Keeper activity.
